issues.description: Method addGuestStudents: The problem statement and UML specify a public method addGuestStudents(int) that takes a single int parameter and returns void (problem_statement.md lines 49-51 and UML lines 72-73). The solution implementation provides public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents) (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java line 90). The template, however, declares public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents, boolean validateInput) (template_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java line 19), i.e. a two-parameter signature with an extra boolean. This parameter-list mismatch between the template and the specification/solution will confuse students about the required API and can cause tests or example usage that expect addGuestStudents(int) to fail or require students to add an overloaded method instead of implementing the specified signature.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the template's public API match the problem statement and solution. Change the method declaration in template_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java to: public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents) { ... } (implement validation inside if needed). Alternatively, provide an overloaded single-argument public void addGuestStudents(int) that delegates to the existing two-argument method, and remove the unexpected boolean parameter from the public API so it matches the UML and instructions.
